item.title: naming things in practice
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I spent a while getting naming things wrong. Here is the version that works for me.

why it matters

Naming things shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.
  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: what i learned about naming things
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I keep coming back to naming things, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Naming things shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: on naming things
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Every few months naming things bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Naming things shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
